title: Standing Calf Raise
summary: A calf raise with straight knees, so the gastrocnemius works from a deep stretch. The library rates gastrocnemius 1 and soleus 0.7.

equipment_needs.text: Needs: commercial gym machine (this exercise's own machine).

muscles.why: Both calf muscles point the foot (plantarflexion). The gastrocnemius also crosses the knee, so with straight legs it stays long and does most of the work (gastroc 1, soleus 0.7).

region_notes.text: Standing calf raises grew the gastrocnemius far more than seated raises in a 12-week study; soleus growth was similar.

setup.text: Set the shoulder pads so your legs are straight with the balls of your feet on the edge of the platform.
Feet about hip width, toes forward or slightly out.
Hold the handles and stand tall with your knees straight but not forced back.

form_cues.cue: Lower to a deep heel stretch
form_cues.why: The bottom stretch is where the gastrocnemius is longest.
A one-second pause removes the stretch reflex bounce, so the muscle does the work.

form_cues.cue: Rise as high as you can
form_cues.why: Full height finishes the rep through the whole range.

form_cues.cue: Pause in the bottom stretch for a second. Bouncing skips most of the benefit.
form_cues.why: Bounce reps shorten the hard part of the range.
Keeps the ankle from rolling out to the little toe at the top.

bias_tweaks.change: Bias the bottom half (lengthened partials) at the end of a set
bias_tweaks.effect: Calf-raise partials in the stretched range grew the gastrocnemius more than partials near the top.
bias_tweaks.caveat: Full range with a pause is still the default.

bias_tweaks.change: Bend the knees (seated calf raise) to shift work to the soleus
bias_tweaks.effect: A bent knee slackens the gastrocnemius, so the soleus does more.
bias_tweaks.caveat: Seated raises barely grew the gastrocnemius in that study, so keep standing raises for it.

bias_tweaks.change: Lower in 2-3 seconds and pause briefly in the stretch
bias_tweaks.effect: Keeps tension on in the lengthened position and removes bounce, so each rep starts honestly.
bias_tweaks.caveat: Rep speeds from 0.5 to 8 s gave similar growth; this is a control tool, not a growth trick.

mistakes.fix: Slow down, pause in the stretch and use the full height every rep.

mistakes.text: Bending the knees to push the weight up.
mistakes.fix: Keep the knees straight; reduce the load.

mistakes.text: Heels never dropping below the platform.
mistakes.fix: Stand far enough back that the heel can drop into a stretch.

misconceptions.myth: Toes in or out builds the inner or outer calf.
misconceptions.reality: Foot angle changes EMG a little; there is no solid growth evidence for it. Pick a comfortable stance.

misconceptions.myth: Seated and standing calf raises do the same thing.
misconceptions.reality: Standing raises grew the gastrocnemius far more; soleus growth was similar.

lower_risk.text: The app adds no ramp-up sets here. If the muscle is not warm from earlier work, make the first set a little lighter.

Add load in small steps. The app suggests a heavier load only when the jump is 10% or less; otherwise it adds a rep first, up to 2 past the top of the range. Default steps for this equipment are 2.5 kg or 5 lb; your gym profile can replace them.
Aim for about 2 reps in reserve in the 10-15 rep range. Calf sets feel brutal near failure; keep the pause and the depth even on the last reps.
Lower slowly into the stretch and pause; don't drop into it.
The shoulder pads load the spine (swap tag 'Loads the spine'). If that doesn't suit you, use the leg-press calf raise.

alternatives.why: Same straight-knee calf work without the load on your shoulders.
No spinal load, but bent knees shift the work to the soleus.

notes: The standing-vs-seated result is one 12-week study in 14 untrained adults.
Ratings and display bands are the library model (main >= 0.75, helper 0.4 to < 0.75, minor 0.25 to < 0.4, not counted < 0.25).
Technique and load management only. This page makes no medical or injury claims.
